newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends week tad lower.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends week tad lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed on Friday a scant 0.09 percent lower with the listing of credit firm Maghrebail the focus of today's session, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 637.42 from 638.02 points on Thursday.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir edged down two dirhams to 356 dirhams.

Blue-chip Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed unchanged at 860 dirhams from last week. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed at 579 dirhams from 588 dirhams. Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie dropped eight dirhams to 481 dirhams.
The bank recently said it would increase its capital to 742.50 million dirhams ($78.16 million) from 618.75 million dirhams through a new share issue.
Subscriptions would be open from July 14 to 28.
The first and second tranche of privatisation bonds, issued in January and May 1996 rose 12 dirhams to 1,371 dirhams and 29 dirhams to 1,199 dirhams.
First Moroccan private conglomerate, ONA Group rose 10 dirhams to 775 dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, the second largest private group, gained nine dirhams to 729 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid advanced 10 dirhams to 540 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 25.7 million dirhams from 24.7 million.
On the over-the-counter market, volume was 48.4 million dirhams from 42.9 million.
